git_basics.notes: Exceptional hands-on performance. Completed repository initialization, staging, committing, and history inspection with professional-grade commit messages. Understands three-state model deeply. Ready for advanced Git workflows (branching, merging, GitHub integration).

terminal_comfort.notes: Demonstrated fluency with ls, cd, mkdir, echo, touch, git commands. Problem-solving flexibility shown (echo vs touch). Ready for more complex terminal workflows (pipes, redirects, scripting).

markdown_documentation.notes: Created comprehensive README.md with proper markdown formatting (headers, lists, code blocks). Documented project vision, features, tech stack professionally. Portfolio-ready documentation skills.

project_organization.notes: Proactively created .gitignore for Python/Node artifacts. Understands importance of repository cleanliness. Ready for more complex project structures (src/ directories, config files, documentation folders).

technical_vocabulary.notes: Expanded vocabulary: working directory, staging area, commit ID (SHA-1), HEAD, tracked/untracked files, Conventional Commits. Strong command of Git-specific terminology.

systems_thinking.notes: Demonstrated understanding of Git's three-state model architecture. Recognized importance of staging area for logical history. Identified continuity patterns (notes.txt observation). Shows architectural awareness.

commit_message_writing.notes: Professional-grade commit messages following Conventional Commits format (feat, docs, chore types). Uses imperative mood, keeps messages concise (<50 chars), provides clear scope. Portfolio-ready commit history.
